ads.headline: Promises, made real
ads.body:
Life doesn’t always go as planned. Our promise is to be there when it doesn’t. Over the last five years, S$5.2 billion in claims went to supporting people through life’s unexpected moments. 

#PromisesMadeReal #HereWhenItMatters

Treatment has an end date. Recovery may not.⁠
⁠
Daniel completed six months of chemotherapy, but it took roughly a year from diagnosis before he felt strong enough to exercise again. His laptop remained untouched for four months.⁠
⁠
Prudential Singapore’s Health Gap Years poll found that 67% of respondents expected severe-stage critical illness recovery to take more than a year.⁠
⁠
Your health may put work on pause. Your bills probably won’t.⁠
⁠
Could your finances handle a Health Gap Year?⁠
⁠
Watch Daniel’s full story on YouTube.⁠
⁠
Disclaimer: This content is for general information only and is not medical or financial advice. Costs and insurance coverage differ by person and policy. Speak to qualified healthcare and financial professionals for advice specific to you.⁠
⁠
#TheFinancialCoconut #ChillsWithTFC #Prudential #PrudentialSingapore #HealInYourHealthGapYears #CriticalIllness

ads.headline: The Financial Coconut
ads.body:
Before cancer, Daniel from @SGFireCouple admits that he was obsessed with money. Between leading a sales team, trading during US market hours and pursuing multiple income streams, being busy made him feel successful—and success became his identity.⁠
⁠
His diagnosis of stage 2B classical Hodgkin lymphoma at 34 dismantled that identity overnight. Instead of asking how much he could earn, Daniel began wondering whether the money he built for his daughters mattered if he could not be present with them.⁠
⁠
Daniel was fortunate to have breathing room. His employer continued paying his salary for six months, while hospitalisation and early Critical Illness coverage supported his treatment and other needs.⁠
⁠
Recovery costs are not limited to hospital bills. They can include transport, caregiving, dietary changes and loss of income. For Daniel, healing meant leaving corporate life and rebuilding his identity around health, family and presence.⁠
⁠
Hit the link in bio now to watch our full episode with Daniel now!⁠
⁠
Disclaimer: This content is for general information only and is not medical or financial advice. Costs, recovery experiences and insurance coverage differ by person and policy. Speak to qualified healthcare and financial professionals before making any decisions.⁠
⁠
#Prudential #HealInYourHealthGapYears #health

ads.headline: Schedule Your Literacy Assessment with MindChamps Reading @ Toa Payoh Central Today
ads.body:
Preschool parents, did you know MOE has already defined the expected standards for your child’s reading ability? Here’s what it says:

By the end of Kindergarten 2, MOE's Nurturing Early Learners Framework requires every child to be able to: 

- Blend and segment individual sounds in words 
- Recognise high-frequency sight words
- Read short sentences from familiar materials 
- Retell and sequence story events
- Construct meaning from texts using picture cues and prior knowledge. 

In other words, your child needs to do more than sound out words. MOE expects your child to understand what they are reading.

Most parents do not know this list exists, and most preschool reading programmes do not intentionally build every skill here as well. They focus on phonics and letter recognition, which covers only part of what MOE defines as reading readiness. 

The other skills, including comprehension, story sequencing, and active meaning-making, are left to develop on their own. By the time the gap becomes visible, your child is already in Primary 1.

The only way to know where your child actually stands is to measure them against these dimensions of reading readiness, not just the ones that are easiest to see.

That is exactly what the MindChamps Literacy Assessment was built to do.

At MindChamps Reading, our Literacy Assessment is specially designed by our in-house team of early childhood literacy experts. This will provide an accurate measure of your child’s current reading ability.

Knowing your child’s current competencies in language will indicate where your child needs to improve.

Our MindChamps Reading programme nurtures 8 critical skills in children to help them with their learning and also nurture their love for reading. They are: 

1. Engagement 
2. Active Understanding 
3. Narrative Intelligence & Higher-Order Thinking Skills 
4. Phonemic Awareness 
5. Phonics 
6. Fluency 
7. Vocabulary-Building 
8. Structural Awareness

After the assessment, we will walk you through your child’s results and share tips on how you can help them to improve.

Schedule your child’s literacy assessment at the MindChamps Reading centre closest to your home today!

Supporting your child’s most precious years,
MindChamps Reading team

P.S. Here’s what other parents say about MindChamps Reading:

“Since Felicia started attending reading lessons at MindChamps, she has improved in the way she communicates, as well as in her pronunciation of words.

“I am especially attracted to the programme because it adopts a comprehensive approach to cultivating a child’s reading skills. More importantly, Felicia truly enjoys attending her lessons and always looks forward to her weekly class.

“The trainers at MindChamps are very professional and I am amazed at their ability to handle children, especially in getting them to settle down and pay attention in class.”

– Hong Yuqun, parent of Felicia Chin Yu Xuan

“We have seen tremendous progress and improvement in Sonya after enrolling her for the programmes at MindChamps.

“From a preschooler who could hardly read a complete sentence, she now reads with ease just 6 months after starting the MindChamps Reading programme. The programme has also helped to strengthen her foundation in phonics, which in turn made her really adept in spelling.”

– Bryan Lim, parent of Sonya Lim

ads.headline: Book an appointment
ads.body:
Heavy periods, bloating that won't settle, or a dull pelvic ache you've learned to live with? These are often written off as "just part of the cycle", but they can also point to uterine fibroids or ovarian cysts. 🩺

They're two of the most common gynaecological conditions in women, and while they're often confused, they're not the same thing. The good news is that both are very manageable when picked up early.

Some conditions may affect fertility if left untreated, so it's worth understanding what your body is telling you. 💗

✨ Schedule an appointment with a gynaecologist today.

Special thanks to Dr Wang Junjie, Thomson Women's Clinic & Cancer Surgery (Novena), for reviewing this content.
